lead: More generated output is not the same as more completed work or more publisher traffic. New reporting shifts attention to review queues, search clicks and the boundaries around code execution.

sections.title: Search clicks and the cost of review
sections.intro: Desktop search experiments and engineering-adoption studies measure different downstream effects. Their samples and identification limits matter.

sections.title: Separating generated code from its executor
sections.intro: An external sandbox design narrows one execution boundary, while split inference assigns prompt processing and response generation to different hardware.

sections.title: Launch demonstrations and inaccessible details
sections.intro: Author-run examples add context to release claims. Unreadable model and video announcements leave practical terms unverified.

sections.title: Paper wealth is not committed capital
sections.intro: Indexed reporting about insider valuations and selective infrastructure investment cannot establish realized proceeds or future commitments.

sections.title: An attributed explanation for the outages
sections.intro: Anonymous-source reporting connects some disruptions with hurried patching, while incident-specific forensic confirmation remains unavailable.

sections.title: The publisher behind a falling traffic chart
sections.intro: A first-person account adds livelihood and reader relationships to the search-click debate, without isolating every cause.

sections.title: Security friction and social connection
sections.intro: An institutional critique and a youth survey address different human costs. Neither establishes a simple causal effect of AI.

sections.title: Office agents and the data behind them
sections.intro: Editable application outputs, governance promises and multimodal data infrastructure come with distinct verification needs.

sections.title: Timing complaints, creative interfaces and projected returns
sections.intro: A short private-evaluation excerpt, a code-heavy application page and inaccessible financial reporting support only bounded conclusions.

sections.title: Learning energy and writing weights
sections.intro: Bounded reasoning benchmarks and hand-engineered networks expose useful mechanisms without proving a general replacement for training.

sections.title: Durable work is not a verified outcome
sections.intro: Queues, workflow recovery, mission budgets and model confidence address different pieces of reliable agent execution.

sections.title: Delegation raises a data boundary question
sections.intro: Expanded task execution and a call for data minimization put convenience and authorized scope in direct tension.

sections.title: Robotics data and authored characters
sections.intro: First-person training data and constrained animatronics are distinct paths toward systems acting in physical environments.

sections.title: Authorship and consciousness remain contested
sections.intro: Detector scores cannot adjudicate literary authorship, and philosophical objections are not experimental consciousness tests.

sections.title: Board decisions, negotiations and proposed rules
sections.intro: A conditional return offer, investment regret and reported policy discussions must remain distinct from completed decisions.

sections.title: Model speed and generated worlds
sections.intro: New Google releases combine benchmark claims with different access tiers and explicit research limits.

sections.title: From audit questions to maintained software
sections.intro: A parallel audit trial, software factories and rewrite critiques distinguish activity from independently reliable outcomes.

sections.title: Infrastructure reaches beyond the sandbox
sections.intro: Open-table indexes and environment lifecycles solve different constraints, while draft approval remains a claim to test.

sections.title: Scanner identity is not a user-agent string
sections.intro: Observed probes for exposed configuration do not establish who controls a scanner, and vulnerability reports still need official advisories.

sections.title: Offering prices, ownership and opposition
sections.intro: Updated pricing reports, convertible ownership and advocacy need different standards from completed trading or adjudicated findings.

sections.title: Questions about education and cognition
sections.intro: An episode description and a short metaphor do not establish measured educational or cognitive effects.
